def main(input_grid):
    # Plan:
    # 1. Identify all connected components in the grid.
    # 2. Translate each component downwards until it hits an obstacle or the grid boundary.

    output_grid = input_grid.copy()
    width, height = input_grid.shape

    # We iterate over all colors except black
    for color in Color.NOT_BLACK:
        # Find all connected components of this color
        visited = np.zeros_like(output_grid, dtype=bool)

        for x, y in np.argwhere(output_grid == color):
            if visited[x, y]:
                continue
            
            # Extract the connected component
            component = np.zeros_like(output_grid)
            to_visit = [(x, y)]
            
            while to_visit:
                cx, cy = to_visit.pop()
                if visited[cx, cy] or output_grid[cx, cy] != color:
                    continue
                
                visited[cx, cy] = True
                component[cx, cy] = color

                # Check 4-way connectivity
                for nx, ny in [(cx-1, cy), (cx+1, cy), (cx, cy-1), (cx, cy+1)]:

                        to_visit.append((nx, ny))
            
            # Translate the component downwards
            while True:
                translated_component = translate(component, x=0, y=1, background=Color.BLACK)
                if contact(object1=translated_component, object2=output_grid, connectivity=4):
                    break
                component = translated_component
            
            # Blit the translated component back onto the output grid
            blit_object(output_grid, component, background=Color.BLACK)

    return output_grid

def main(input_grid):
    # The output grid starts as a copy of the input grid, so we can modify it.
    output_grid = input_grid.copy()
    width, height = input_grid.shape

    # Iterate over each colored component (excluding black and gray)
    for color in Color.NOT_BLACK - {Color.GRAY}:
        # Find all the connected components of the current color
        component_positions = np.argwhere(input_grid == color)

        if len(component_positions) == 0:
            continue

        # For each component, simulate gravity by translating it downward
        max_y_translation = 0

        for (x, y) in component_positions:
            # Calculate how far it can fall until it hits an obstacle or the boundary
            distance = 0
            while y + distance + 1 < height and (output_grid[x, y + distance + 1] == Color.BLACK):
                distance += 1

            # Update max_y_translation as the minimum distance all parts of the component can fall
            max_y_translation = min(distance, max_y_translation) if max_y_translation else distance

        # Translate the entire component down by max_y_translation
        for (x, y) in component_positions:
            output_grid[x, y] = Color.BLACK
            output_grid[x, y + max_y_translation] = color

    return output_grid

# description:
# In the input grid, you will see various colored objects suspended in mid-air above a ground.
# To create the output grid, apply gravity to all objects, meaning translate each object downward until it rests on the ground or another object without overlapping.

def main(input_grid):
    # Copy the input grid to start forming the output grid
    output_grid = np.copy(input_grid)

    # Find all connected components in the grid
    objects = find_connected_components(input_grid, background=Color.BLACK, connectivity=4, monochromatic=True)

    # Sort objects by their bottommost y-coordinate to apply gravity properly
    def bottommost_y(obj):
        _, y, _, h = bounding_box(obj, background=Color.BLACK)
        return y + h - 1
    
    objects.sort(key=bottommost_y, reverse=True)

    # Apply gravity to each object
    for obj in objects:
        sprite = crop(obj, background=Color.BLACK)
        x, y, _, _ = bounding_box(obj, background=Color.BLACK)

        # Move the object down until it collides with another object or the grid bottom
        while True:
            if collision(output_grid, sprite, x2=x, y2=y + 1, background=Color.BLACK):
                break
            y += 1

        # Place the object at its final position
        blit_sprite(output_grid, sprite, x, y, background=Color.BLACK)

    return output_grid

def generate_input():

        while True:

            # Check for collision with boundaries or obstacles
            if new_x < 0 or new_y < 0 or new_x + sprite.shape[0] > output_grid.shape[0] or new_y + sprite.shape[1] > output_grid.shape[1]:

            if collision(object1=output_grid, object2=sprite, x2=new_x, y2=new_y, background=Color.BLACK):

            # Move the component

def main(input_grid):

    # Copy the input grid to the output grid
    output_grid = np.copy(input_grid)
    
    # Identify the obstacles in the grid
    obstacle_color = Color.GREY
    block_colors = set(Color.NOT_BLACK) - {obstacle_color}

    # Process each column separately
    for col in range(cols):
        # Extract the column and reverse it for easier gravity effect processing
        column = output_grid[:, col][::-1]
        
        # Initialize indices for placing blocks
        place_index = 0
        
        # Traverse the column to apply gravity
        for idx, cell in enumerate(column):
            if cell in block_colors:
                # Place the block as far down as possible
                column[place_index] = cell
                place_index += 1
            elif cell == obstacle_color:
                # Reset the place index after hitting an obstacle
                place_index = idx + 1
        
        # Fill remaining spaces with black
        for i in range(place_index, len(column)):
            column[i] = Color.BLACK
        
        # Reverse back to the original order and update the output grid
        output_grid[:, col] = column[::-1]
    
    return output_grid

def main(input_grid, direction):
    # Initialize the output grid
    output_grid = np.copy(input_grid)
    
    block_colors = set(Color.ALL_COLORS) - {Color.BLACK, Color.GREY}  # assuming obstacles are grey
    obstacle_color = Color.GREY
    background = Color.BLACK
    
    # Translate all blocks in the specified direction
    dx, dy = direction
    
    def is_within_bounds(x, y):
        return 0 <= x < output_grid.shape[0] and 0 <= y < output_grid.shape[1]
    
    def can_move(x, y):
        return is_within_bounds(x, y) and output_grid[x, y] == background
    
    # Find all blocks
    for obj in find_connected_components(input_grid, connectivity=4, monochromatic=True, background=obstacle_color):
        obj_color = obj[obj != background][0]
        if obj_color not in block_colors:
            continue  # skip obstacles
        
        # Find the bounding box of the block
        x, y, width, height = bounding_box(obj, background=background)
        
        # Move block in the specified direction until it hits an obstacle or boundary
        while True:
            new_x, new_y = x + dx, y + dy
            if all(can_move(new_x + i, new_y + j) for i in range(width) for j in range(height)):
                x, y = new_x, new_y
            else:
                break
        
        # Blit the block to the new position in the output grid
        blit_sprite(output_grid, obj, x, y, background=background)

    return output_grid
